title: Operator Instrumentation Journey — Audit, Lightweight Widgets, and Trace Handoff
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a lightweight operational playbook intended for operator-facing instrumention work: an audit checklist for existing dashboards, a small curated widget catalogue, and a concrete trace-handoff protocol for root-cause investigations. Target audience: oncall SREs, platform engineers, and feature owners who need pragmatic rules rather than a full taxonomy.

Why this exists (motivation):
- We have too many panels with overlapping signals and high query cost.
- Junior oncallers often lack a clear trace handoff step to engineering on regressions.
- Instrumentation drift: metrics created during experiments never retired.

High-level approach:
1) Audit-first: quick 30-minute audit per dashboard to mark must-keep/merge/delete.
2) Curate: provide 8 low-cost, high-signal widgets for inference path investigations.
3) Standardize trace handoff: short reproducible steps, example queries, and a severity mapping.

30-minute dashboard audit checklist (use as a template) — "fast pass":
- Owner verified: who will pay query cost? (tag the PI)
- Primary SLI exists and matches intent (yes/no)
- Redundant panels: mark panels with >80% overlap (query similarity)
- Query cost estimate: low/medium/high (use query-runner to estimate)
- Alert coverage: does each critical SLI have an alert? (Y/N)
- User journey mapping: can an oncaller reconstruct a user request -> token path in <8 clicks?
- Retirement candidate? (list reason)

Metric maturity rubric (three stages):
- Stage 0 — experimental: ad-hoc, no owner, TTL 30d, high-cardinality permitted.
- Stage 1 — operational: assigned owner, SLI defined, sampled traces available.
- Stage 2 — product-grade: documented SLA, low-cardinality aggregate, costing guardrails, alerting and runbooks.

Curated widget catalogue (8 compact widgets) — lightweight queries, low-cardinality where possible:
1) Per-tenant 95th token-latency (bucketed) — aggregated by tenant label, 1m rollup.
2) Cold KV-cache miss rate (%) — normalized by requests hitting cold state.
3) Inference fanout ratio — model-fanout / request count (high values indicate multi-model routing).
4) Active KV cache size vs eviction rate — correlate evictions with latency spikes.
5) Failed-internal-retries by model variant — short list to identify degradations.
6) Token generation volume / second (total) — telemetry for cost-pacing.
7) Sampling coverage gauge — percent of requests with full trace.
8) Recent rollout vs error delta — aligned to deployment timestamps.

Trace handoff protocol (three-step template):
1) Reproduce: provide an exact API call (route, headers, input length, pinned model/version) and time window.
2) Attach compact traces: include request-id, span ids, and a 1–2 sentence hypothesis (e.g., "KV cache miss at shard 3 caused 2x latency").
3) Severity + next action: map to severity (sev1: customer-facing outage — page oncall team / sev2: degraded SLO — create incident ticket and assign owner / sev3: non-urgent tuning).

Example trace payload to include in tickets (copyable):
- api_route: /v1/generate
- request_id: rqc-20260208-9a2b
- model: redwood-7b-quant
- seq_len: 1024
- observed_95_latency_ms: 740
- hypothesis: "High KV eviction at node-7 around T triggered cache re-warm and increased latency"

Query-cost and dashboard budgeting guidance:
- Classify dashboards as: cheap (monthly cost < $25), moderate ($25-$200), expensive (> $200).
- Enforce query-rate quotas for expensive panels (throttle at 6 queries/min per panel).
- Replace high-cardinality panels with sampled panels + drilldowns.

Onboarding checklist for a new operator:
- Quick tour: 10-minute walkthrough of the curated widgets and where to find runbooks.
- Playbook digest: 1-page laminated PDF for the oncall desk (include 3 bookmarks: SLI lookup, trace handoff snippet, rollback link).
- Simulation: run one synthetic canary failover and practice creating a ticket with the trace payload template.

Open questions and next steps:
- Can we automate the 30-minute audit using query-similarity heuristics? (proto: use cosine on query strings).
- Add a cheap-sampled trace sink for dev tenants to boost sampling coverage without high cost.
- Create a migration plan to move Stage 0 metrics to TTL-based archives after 60 days.

Appendix: quick metric definitions (operator-facing):
- token_latency_95_p50: "95th percentile per-token latency measured across requests, 1m rollup, excluding backend retries"
- kv_cache_miss_ratio: "(misses / (hits + misses)) sampled over 1m, label by tenant, shard"
- model_fanout_ratio: "sum(model_invocations) / sum(requests) over 5m, indicates multi-model expansion"

Notes to self (todo):
- Draft the laminated digest and hand to oncall at next rotation.
- Run audit on top-10 expensive dashboards this quarter.
- Prototype sampled-trace sink and measure cost delta.

If you pick this up: start with the audit template on dashboard-list JIRA. Use the linked artifacts above as anchors.

End of doc."
